clue.text: Need to hold marines back for airborne advance

indicators.note: the word for need wraps round, holding, the other pieces inside it

parts.note: to need is to want
RM is the Royal Marines
back as in to and fro, where fro means backwards

explanation.surface: A military plan: troops must keep the marines in reserve to support a parachute assault.
explanation.walkthrough: The military surface hides a weather term: an 'airborne advance' is a mass of air moving forward, not paratroops.
explanation.definitionFit: In meteorology a front is the leading edge of an advancing air mass, here the warmer one.

clue.text: Initially, Gilbert holds back blows

indicators.note: the initials wrap round the other piece, holding it in the middle

parts.note: W. S. Gilbert, the librettist of Gilbert and Sullivan, goes by the initials WS
aft means at the back of a ship

explanation.surface: The librettist Gilbert, in the opening exchanges, absorbs punches without hitting back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Initially' points to Gilbert's initials WS rather than his first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Wafts and blows are both verbs for air or wind carrying something gently along.

clue.text: My husband and I? Just I

definitions.text: My husband and I? Just I

parts.words: My husband and I? Just I
parts.note: the Queen's famous phrase My husband and I sounds plural, but the monarch's plural pronoun refers to a single person

explanation.surface: A wry correction: the speaker who says 'my husband and I' really only means herself.
explanation.walkthrough: The royal we is the plural pronoun a monarch uses for themselves; 'My husband and I' was Queen Elizabeth II's well-known opening phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase names the plural pronoun a sovereign uses while meaning only themselves.

clue.text: Dither, as a female among others

indicators.note: the pieces sit among, between, the letters of the abbreviation for others

parts.note: ff. is the abbreviation for 'and following', the pages after the one cited

explanation.surface: Someone hesitating like a lone woman unsure of herself in a crowd.
explanation.walkthrough: 'others' is ff., the reference abbreviation for 'and the following pages'.
explanation.definitionFit: To faff, a British colloquialism, is to waste time fussing about indecisively.

clue.text: In the grass, succeeded getting sexual satisfaction

parts.note: the oat is a cereal grass
S is the abbreviation for succeeded, used in genealogies

explanation.surface: A tryst in the long grass that ended happily.
explanation.walkthrough: Getting one's oats is British slang for having sex.
explanation.definitionFit: The slang phrase 'getting your oats' means obtaining sexual gratification.

clue.text: Group on which policeman may be shortly in case

parts.note: a patrolling officer is said to be on the beat

indicators.note: shortly says the word is cut short, losing its final letter

parts.note: lest means in case, for fear that

explanation.surface: A band that a patrolling constable might soon investigate.
explanation.definitionFit: The Liverpool foursome are the most famous pop group of all, a group in the musical sense.

clue.text: Black tie initially discarded by firm

indicators.note: the opening letter of tie is thrown out of the word for firm

parts.note: stable means firm, steady

indicators.note: initially picks out the first letter of the word tie

explanation.surface: An office dress code where a company drops its black-tie requirement.
explanation.definitionFit: Sable is the heraldic term for the colour black, also used poetically.

clue.text: Bangs up doctor feeding jerks stimulating pills

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the word is written bottom to top, backwards

parts.note: rams means bangs into, strikes hard

indicators.note: the doctor's abbreviation goes into, feeding, the word for jerks

parts.note: tugs means jerks, pulls sharply

explanation.surface: A doctor locks up patients who are twitching after taking stimulants.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'up' reads the word bottom to top; 'feeding' puts the doctor inside the word for jerks.
explanation.definitionFit: Smart drugs are nootropics, pills taken to boost concentration and mental performance.

clue.text: Lad just penetrated by tip of weapon that's piercing

indicators.note: the dart only just goes in: its tip slips between the lad's last two letters while the rest stays outside

parts.note: a lad is a boy
a dart is a small thrown weapon

explanation.surface: A boy is barely nicked by the point of a weapon, a painful piercing.
explanation.walkthrough: Only the dart's tip goes in: D slips between BO and Y, and the rest of the dart, ART, stays outside. A piercing is one kind of body art.
explanation.definitionFit: Ear, nose and navel piercings are a type of decorative skin modification, like tattoos.

clue.text: Swindle by priest — you cover it up, that's all

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the whole construction is read from the bottom, backwards
the old word for you goes round the other pieces, covering them

parts.note: ye is an old form of you
to do someone is to swindle them
Rev is short for Reverend, a priest's title

explanation.surface: A con by a clergyman, and you hush it up: that's the full story.
explanation.walkthrough: YE is the archaic you. 'cover it' wraps it round the other pieces, and 'up' reads the lot bottom to top in this down clue.
explanation.definitionFit: Everyone together is all the people, so the pronoun 'all' can stand for the whole lot.

clue.text: Leave by plane: deal with article first, or lose it

parts.note: to fly off is to depart by aircraft
the is the definite article
to handle is to deal with

explanation.surface: Travel instructions: fly out, sort the paperwork first, or lose the plot.
explanation.definitionFit: Both idioms mean to suddenly lose one's temper.

clue.text: Hear such music unaccompanied

indicators.note: hear says the word for the music is to be said aloud, giving a word of the same sound

parts.note: soul is a style of music

explanation.surface: An invitation to listen to some solo music.
explanation.definitionFit: Sole means single or only, alone without a companion.

clue.text: Relax: everything difficult has been done?

definitions.meaning: to relax is to stop worrying and sleep soundly
read literally, the rest of the job is easy since the hard part is over

explanation.surface: Reassurance: take it easy, the hard work is finished.
explanation.walkthrough: The second reading takes 'rest' as the remainder: the rest is easy.
explanation.definitionFit: To be untroubled is to relax; literally the remaining part of the work is now simple.

clue.text: Stopped selling members-only arrangement

definitions.meaning: a store that has ceased trading has shut its doors
a workplace where only union members may be employed

explanation.surface: A shop that stopped trading and became exclusive.
explanation.walkthrough: In British industrial relations, a closed shop is a firm where all workers must belong to a trade union.
explanation.definitionFit: A store shut for business; also a union arrangement restricting employment to members.

clue.text: Loose regulation of a branch of medicine

indicators.note: loose regulation is slack and disordered, so its letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A complaint about lax rules in one medical specialty.
explanation.definitionFit: Urogenital medicine deals with the urinary and reproductive organs, a recognised specialty.

clue.text: Have suspicion stream all polluted

indicators.note: polluted water is fouled up, so the letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: Someone suspects the whole river has been contaminated.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means to sense that something is wrong or underhand.

clue.text: Curling lip, a snob's finding this on tea tray?

indicators.note: a curling lip is twisted, so the letters are twisted into a new order

explanation.surface: A snob sneers at the dish found on the tea tray.
explanation.walkthrough: A slop basin is a bowl on a tea set for tipping out cold dregs, the kind of thing a snob might disdain.
explanation.definitionFit: A slop basin is a bowl kept on a tea tray to receive tea dregs and leaves.

clue.text: Looking back, hospital worker retired, leaving quietly

indicators.note: the quiet letter leaves, being dropped from the end
retired means drawn back, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: a porter moves patients round a hospital
p (piano) is the musical marking for quietly

explanation.surface: A hospital porter quietly retires, glancing back as he leaves.
explanation.walkthrough: 'retired' turns PORTER into RETROP; 'leaving' drops the P.
explanation.definitionFit: Retro styles imitate or hark back to the fashions of the past.

clue.text: Hears appeal to Islamic leaders

parts.note: O is an exclamation of appeal, as in 'O Lord'
beys were Ottoman governors and chiefs

explanation.surface: Someone listens to a plea addressed to Muslim chiefs.
explanation.definitionFit: To hear an instruction, in the sense of heeding it, is to comply with it.

clue.text: Distinguished artist seen on Tate Modern visit at last

parts.note: Tracey Emin is a well-known British artist

indicators.note: at last picks the final letter of each of the three words

explanation.surface: A famous artist spotted at the end of a gallery visit.
explanation.walkthrough: Tate Modern is London's modern art gallery, where Emin has exhibited.
explanation.definitionFit: Eminent and distinguished are synonyms for highly respected and famous.

clue.text: I go ahead, not straight (keeping right twice), boy leading

parts.note: Glen is a boy's name

indicators.note: the word for not straight keeps the other letters inside it

parts.note: gay means not heterosexual, not straight

indicators.note: twice means the letter is written two times

explanation.surface: Cryptic directions: I lead on, going crooked, keeping right twice, with a boy in front.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue speaks as the answer: a glengarry is a Scottish cap, so 'I go ahead' means I go on a head.
explanation.definitionFit: A glengarry is a brimless Scottish woollen cap, an item worn on the head.

clue.text: Cameron's extraordinary affair

indicators.note: extraordinary means out of the ordinary, so the name's letters are rearranged

parts.note: the name Cameron, with the 's read as is

explanation.surface: A former prime minister's surprising love life.
explanation.definitionFit: A romance is a love affair, a relationship between lovers.

clue.text: Half-swearing, compulsory to include 'ell, say

indicators.note: the word for compulsory includes the letter within it

parts.note: binding means obligatory, compulsory
the letter L is spelt ell; the apostrophe also hints at a dropped h in hell

explanation.surface: A mild curse that must include 'ell, as said by someone dropping their aitches.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Effing and blinding' is British slang for swearing; this is half of that phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: In the phrase for cursing, effing and blinding, this word is one of the two halves.

clue.text: Like to secure second book

indicators.note: the word for like holds the other piece securely within it

parts.note: as means like, in the manner of
a mo is a moment, a second

explanation.surface: Someone wants to reserve a second volume.
explanation.definitionFit: Amos is a book of the Old Testament, named after a prophet.

clue.text: River that's spilled over track

indicators.note: over means turned over, so the letters run backwards

parts.note: oops is what someone says when a drink is spilt

explanation.surface: A river has burst its banks and flooded a path.
explanation.walkthrough: 'over' turns R plus OOPS into SPOOR.
explanation.definitionFit: Spoor is the trail or droppings an animal leaves, which hunters follow.

clue.text: Hitch small horse

parts.note: a nag is a horse, often an old one

explanation.surface: An instruction to harness a pony.
explanation.definitionFit: A hitch is a problem or obstacle that holds things up.

clue.text: Get away with wordless singing

definitions.meaning: a command to shoo, clear off
improvised jazz vocals using nonsense syllables

explanation.definitionFit: Scat is both an order to leave at once and jazz singing with improvised syllables.

clue.text: Offer doubtful help — we had nothing Cantonese to cook

indicators.note: to cook the books is to rework them, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: the words are taken as written, with nothing becoming O, the zero-shaped letter

explanation.surface: Kitchen hesitancy: we had no Cantonese food to cook.
explanation.definitionFit: Saying you will try your best while promising no result is offering help with uncertain outcome.

clue.text: Umpire's call assumed reversible

indicators.note: reversible means it can be turned back, so the phrase is read backwards

parts.note: put on means assumed, as a manner or garment

explanation.surface: A referee's ruling that could be overturned on appeal.
explanation.walkthrough: In squash and similar games the call 'not up' means the ball bounced twice before being returned.
explanation.definitionFit: An umpire in racket games shouts this when a player fails to reach the ball in time.

clue.text: Great distance I travelled with lethargy

indicators.note: travelled means moved about, so these letters move into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone sluggishly covers a long way.
explanation.definitionFit: A light-year is the distance light covers in a year, an astronomical length.
